MINUTES

  SPECIAL MEETING
  GLENDALE TRANSPORTATION & PARKING COMMISSION
  May 20, 2019

  DATE:  Monday, May 20, 2019
  TIME:  6:00 p.m.
  LOCATION:  City Council Chambers
  613 East Broadway, Glendale CA 91206

The special meeting of the Glendale Transportation and Parking Commission (TPC) of Monday,
May 20, 2019 was called to order at 6:05 p.m.
Commissioner Sahakian sat in as Chair Pro Tem for Chairperson Kurkjian.

1. REGULAR BUSINESS AGENDA
  a. Roll Call- Yacoubian, Sahakian (taking place of Chairperson Kurkjian), Nazarian
  Absent: Gonzalez, Kurkjian
  b. Flag Salute – Chair Pro Tem Sahakian

2. POSTING OF AGENDA
  The agenda for the Monday, May 20, 2019 special meeting of the Glendale
  Transportation & Parking Commission was posted by Thursday, May 16, 2019, before
  5:00 p.m. on the bulletin board outside of City Hall.

3. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS
  Discussion is limited to items NOT a part of this agenda. Each speaker is allowed five
  minutes. The Commission may question the speaker but there will be no debate or
  decision.

4. ACTION
   Receive Presentation and Report regarding Downtown Glendale and Montrose
  Comprehensive Parking Analysis

Assistant Director of Public Works, Edward Hitti, presented this item. Mr. Hitti expressed the
purpose and need to revisit the original 2007 Mobility study as Glendale has exponentially
grown in population, as well as in businesses and activities since 2007. This new study also
included Montrose area, whereas the original study only focused on the Downtown Glendale
area. By revisiting the study, staff was able to review what changes had been implemented,
which would allow staff to assess those changes and make recommendations for any necessary
modifications and improvements. Mr. Hitti introduced the Parking Manager, Mr. Tad Dombroski,
to expound on the recent study conducted by TranspoGroup. Mr. Dombroski mentioned that in
2018, City Council awarded a contract to TranspoGroup to conduct parking related research. In
September of 2018, TranspoGroup began their studies and had recently completed their report
to present to the TPC. Mr. Dombroski introduced Dan McKinney, a Principal at TranspoGroup,
to present their findings. Mr. McKinney explained their approach was a performance based
strategy that relied on data such as parking inventory and occupancy, parking regulations and
restrictions as well as pricing strategies and new innovative payment systems. This study
focused on the Downtown Glendale and Montrose areas. Some of TranspoGroup’s
recommendations for the Downtown area included creating a tiered pricing approach, raising
 the price of parking meters in certain areas, convert some on-street non paid parking to paid
parking, update parking technology, and adjust the timeframe for unpaid parking areas. For the
Montrose area, TranspoGroup recommended similar adjustments to parking but also installation
of parking meters in the parking lots that are currently free and improving wayfinding signage to
reroute drivers to relieve traffic and parking congestion along Honolulu Avenue. Commissioner
Yacoubian asked if parking detection on Brand Boulevard would be viable, Mr. McKinney
informed her that at this point in time, the technology is very expensive and very unreliable
therefore this avenue would not be beneficial to the City of Glendale at this time. Chair Pro Tem
Sahakian recommended not implementing parking detection notification systems as they tend to
encourage traffic recirculation and congestion.

Chair Pro Tem Sahakian proceeded to address the members of the community who came to
voice their concerns regarding the Downtown Glendale and Montrose Parking Analysis report.
Rick Lemmo spoke on behalf of the Greater Downtown Glendale Community Benefit District
and was in favor of the parking study presented by TranspoGroup. He advised the City to look
into ridesharing companies that are becoming more prevalent in cities such as Glendale, and
recommended the study be passed onto City Council for approval.

Andre Ordubegian, president of the Montrose Parking Association, stated that in contrast the
study presented, there is nearly no available street parking in Montrose and neighboring parking
lots number three and seven are always packed. He mentioned the study’s recommendation to
raise parking rates will not only hurt businesses in Montrose, but cause frustration among the
public. He also mentioned that Glendale City College (GCC) had recently purchased a City
Bank building and is expected to house at least 200 students, plus staff and faculty, that will add
to the parking congestion. He complained that neither residents nor merchants in the area were
contacted for their input for the parking analysis and therefore, he does not recommend the
study go to Council for review.

Other members of the community that spoke out against the study going to Council included
Jeannie Bone from the Montrose Shopping Park Board, Ken Grayson, Treasurer for the
Montrose Shopping Park Association, and Greg Astorian, a commercial realtor practicing in
Downtown Glendale.

After hearing the concerns of the public, Chair Pro Tem Sahakian recommended to note and file
this study and report in order to give staff time to reach out to local business and residents to
incorporate their input in the study.

Moved: Sahakian  Seconded: Yacoubian
Roll Call: Yacoubian, Sahakian, Nazarian
Absent: Gonzalez, Kurkjian

5. INFORMATION
   Glendale-Burbank Regional Streetcar Feasibility Study

Bradly Calvert, Assistant Director of Community Development at the City of Glendale, came
before TPC to discuss the scope of work, route alternatives, street impacts and future planning
regarding the streetcar. They are currently creating and testing new route concepts and
analyzing ridership potential and accessibility. He also discussed the advantages and
disadvantages of implementing a streetcar on a busy street such as Brand Blvd. Mr. Calvert
and his team hope to bring their study to the City Council for consideration in July 2019.
 Commissioner Yacoubian voiced her concern that if the streetcar concept went to Council for
review, she would hope the streetcar to be efficient, economical and beneficial, rather than
intrusive to local businesses, residents and visitors. Commissioner Nazarian recommended a
loop route, rather than a bidirectional route in order to pick up passengers on two major streets,
Central Avenue and Brand Boulevard. He also asked how much parking would be eliminated
by replacing the existing lateral parking with parallel parking in order to make room for potential
streetcar stations. Mr. Calvert confirmed that it is estimated to lose about 30%-40% of parking.
Chair Pro Tem Sahakian asked if staff had ever considered an elevated transportation system,
such as a tram or something similar, so as to preserve the transit systems that are already in
place and to preserve parking. He mentioned he himself had proposed an elevated tram
system to the City of Los Angeles which would transport people from the Gateway Plaza to the
Dodger Stadium. He mentioned trams are easy and fast to build and would not eliminate
parking.

6. COMMISSION/STAFF COMMENTS/UPDATES

There were no comments or updates presented by the Commission or staff.

7. ADJOURNMENT

Moved: Yacoubian  Seconded: Nazarian
